The new scoring preserves parents through clone/parametric choices when energy is low or the population is crowded, uses structural exploration when compact healthy genomes face low diversity or population decline, and keeps mixed mutation for high-energy recovery phases. This should reduce unnecessary disruptive mutation while still injecting topology changes after punctuated events.

patch.patch_description: Add a narrow post-crash rescue gate that only activates when the population is contracting, has room to regrow, and diversity is depleted. The current policy defaults entirely to parametric mutation, so it likely misses rare punctuated-event windows where mixed or structural mutation can restore useful variation. This edit keeps parametric dominant during stable/high-health periods, but gives mixed mutation a strong advantage during severe rescue conditions and structural mutation a secondary advantage when genomes are compact enough to absorb topology changes.

Low-energy or declining-population states bias back toward clone/parametric conservation. The scores remain finite, pure jax.numpy expressions and do not inspect rng.

patch.patch_description: Keep the strong parametric default, but add a conservative mixed-mutation escape hatch only when the parent has usable energy/intake, the population is alive but not expanding strongly, and diversity/lineage entropy are low. This targets post-event recovery cases where pure weight tuning may plateau, while preserving the current all-parametric behavior in most ordinary states.

patch.patch_description: This edit keeps parametric mutation as the default productive operator, but adds a narrow recovery gate where mixed mutation can win when the population has room to regrow, diversity is low, the parent is viable, and the genome still has topology capacity. The prior programs selected parametric exclusively, so this avoids broad exploration; it only lets mixed/structural compete during post-event recovery conditions that should improve resource-productivity AUC through useful novelty while preserving survival. Scores remain pure, bounded JAX expressions and ignore rng.

patch.patch_description: Bias offspring selection toward parametric mutation in stable/productive states, but create a bounded rescue gate that can let mixed mutation compete when the population is shrinking, sparse, or low-diversity and the parent has enough energy/intake to propagate useful variation. This preserves the strong all-parametric baseline most of the time while adding a narrow heredity-aware escape path for post-event recovery, where mixed mutation can improve resource-productivity without relying on rng or hidden state.

patch.patch_description: The current policy always selects parametric mutation because mixed never approaches the parametric score. This edit keeps parametric as the default high-performing action, but adds a bounded recovery gate that lets mixed mutation win only when the population is alive, stagnant, low-diversity, and the parent is capable enough to tolerate a larger mutation. Structural remains below mixed and only rises in compact-genome recovery windows, avoiding broad topology churn.
